    </div>

    <!-- Abstract -->
    <div class="info-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-file-alt"></i> Abstract:</strong>
        The Security Operations Center (SOC) analyst role is the most accessible entry point into cybersecurity —
        and one of the fastest paths to a six-figure salary. But the landscape in 2026 is dramatically different
        from even two years ago. AI-driven SOAR platforms automate Tier 1 triage, cloud-native SOCs replace on-prem
        SIEMs, and the skills gap has widened to 3.5 million unfilled positions globally. This guide provides an
        empirical roadmap: what skills actually matter at each tier, which certifications deliver ROI, realistic
        salary benchmarks by location and experience, and the lab exercises that demonstrate competence to hiring
        managers.
    </div>

    <h2 id="landscape">1. The SOC Landscape in 2026</h2>

    <p>The cybersecurity industry faces a paradox: a projected 3.5 million unfilled positions globally (ISC² 2025
        Workforce Study), yet entry-level candidates report difficulty landing their first SOC role. Understanding
        why requires examining how SOCs have evolved.</p>

    <h3>The Modern SOC: What Changed</h3>

    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Aspect</th>
                <th>Traditional SOC (2020)</th>
                <th>Modern SOC (2026)</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Primary SIEM</strong></td>
                <td>On-prem (QRadar, ArcSight)</td>
                <td>Cloud-native (Microsoft Sentinel, Chronicle, Splunk Cloud)</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Alert Volume</strong></td>
                <td>~5,000/day</td>
                <td>~50,000-500,000/day (AI pre-filtered)</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Tier 1 Role</strong></td>
                <td>Manual alert triage</td>
                <td>SOAR-augmented triage + AI validation</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Key Skill</strong></td>
                <td>SIEM query writing</td>
                <td>Detection engineering + cloud security</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Shift Model</strong></td>
                <td>24/7 on-site rotation</td>
                <td>Follow-the-sun + remote hybrid</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Biggest Threat</strong></td>
                <td>Malware, phishing</td>
                <td>AI-generated attacks, supply chain, identity-based attacks</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="warning-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-exclamation-triangle"></i> Reality Check:</strong>
        "SOC Analyst" job postings dropped 12% in 2025 — but "Detection Engineer," "Threat Hunter," and "Cloud
        Security Analyst" postings <em>increased 34%</em>. The role isn't disappearing; it's
        <strong>evolving</strong>. This roadmap prepares you for where the career is going, not where it was.
    </div>

    <h2 id="tier-system">2. The Tier System Explained</h2>

    <div class="architecture-diagram">
        <pre style="color: var(--accent-cyan); margin: 0;">

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │ SOC CAREER PROGRESSION │ ├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤ │ │ │ TIER 3: THREAT HUNTER / ARCHITECT [$110K-$160K+] │ │ ┌─────────────────────────────────┐ 4-6+ years │ │ │ Detection Engineering │ │ │ │ Threat Intelligence │ │ │ │ Purple Team Operations │ │ │ └────────────┬────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ TIER 2: INCIDENT RESPONDER [$75K-$110K] │ │ ┌────────────┴────────────────────┐ 2-4 years │ │ │ Deep Investigation │ │ │ │ Forensic Analysis │ │ │ │ Malware Triage │ │ │ └────────────┬────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ │ TIER 1: ALERT ANALYST [$55K-$75K] │ │ ┌────────────┴────────────────────┐ 0-2 years │ │ │ Alert Triage & Monitoring │ │ │ │ SIEM Dashboard Management │ │ │ │ Ticket Documentation │ │ │ └─────────────────────────────────┘ │ │ │ │ EXIT RAMPS → CISO │ Security Architect │ GRC │ Sales Eng │ └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ 

    <h2 id="tier1">3. Tier 1: Alert Triage & Monitoring</h2>

    <h3>What You Actually Do</h3>
    <p>Tier 1 analysts are the front line. You monitor SIEM dashboards, triage incoming alerts, determine true
        positives vs. false positives, and escalate confirmed incidents. In a modern SOC, SOAR platforms auto-triage
        60-70% of alerts, but you must validate AI decisions and handle edge cases.</p>

    <h4>Daily Responsibilities</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Monitor SIEM dashboards (Splunk, Sentinel, Chronicle) for security events</li>
        <li>Triage alerts: categorize as true positive, false positive, or benign true positive</li>
        <li>Document findings in ticketing systems (ServiceNow, Jira)</li>
        <li>Perform initial IOC lookups (VirusTotal, AbuseIPDB, OTX)</li>
        <li>Escalate confirmed incidents to Tier 2 with context</li>
        <li>Monitor email security alerts (O365 Defender, Proofpoint)</li>
        <li>Validate SOAR playbook outputs and flag edge cases</li>
    </ul>

    <h4>Required Technical Skills</h4>
    <table>
        <thead>
            <tr>
                <th>Skill</th>
                <th>Proficiency Needed</th>
                <th>How to Learn</th>
            </tr>
        </thead>
        <tbody>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Networking (TCP/IP, DNS, HTTP)</strong></td>
                <td class="severity-critical">Critical</td>
                <td>CompTIA Network+, Packet Tracer labs</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Windows/Linux Administration</strong></td>
                <td class="severity-critical">Critical</td>
                <td>Home lab (VirtualBox/VMware), TryHackMe</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>SIEM Query Writing</strong></td>
                <td class="severity-critical">Critical</td>
                <td>Splunk free tier, Sentinel sandbox</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Log Analysis</strong></td>
                <td class="severity-high">High</td>
                <td>Blue Team Labs, LetsDefend</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>MITRE ATT&CK Framework</strong></td>
                <td class="severity-high">High</td>
                <td>attack.mitre.org + mapping exercises</td>
            </tr>
            <tr>
                <td><strong>Basic Scripting (Python/PowerShell)</strong></td>
                <td>Medium</td>
                <td>Automate the Boring Stuff, PS exercises</td>
            </tr>
        </tbody>
    </table>

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Lab: Your First Splunk Query</h3>
        <p>The query every SOC analyst must know — detecting failed login brute-force attempts:</p>
        <pre><code class="language-spl"># Detect brute-force: 10+ failed logins from same IP in 5 minutes

index=auth sourcetype=WinEventLog:Security EventCode=4625 | stats count as failed_attempts, values(TargetUserName) as users by src_ip | where failed_attempts >= 10 | sort -failed_attempts | table src_ip, failed_attempts, users 

# Microsoft Sentinel KQL equivalent
SecurityEvent
| where EventID == 4625
| where TimeGenerated > ago(5m)
| summarize FailedAttempts = count(),
TargetAccounts = make_set(TargetAccount) by IpAddress
| where FailedAttempts >= 10
| sort by FailedAttempts desc

    <h3>Getting Your First Tier 1 Job</h3>
    <div class="success-box">
        <strong><i class="fas fa-check-circle"></i> The Realistic Path (6-12 Months):</strong>
        <ol>
            <li><strong>Month 1-2:</strong> CompTIA Security+ (study + pass exam)</li>
            <li><strong>Month 2-4:</strong> Build a home lab (Splunk free, Security Onion, Windows AD)</li>
            <li><strong>Month 3-5:</strong> Complete 50+ rooms on TryHackMe (SOC Level 1 path)</li>
            <li><strong>Month 4-6:</strong> Participate in CTF competitions (PicoCTF, National Cyber League)</li>
            <li><strong>Month 5-8:</strong> Create a blog/GitHub documenting your labs and investigations</li>
            <li><strong>Month 6-12:</strong> Apply broadly — MSPs, MSSPs, and contract SOC positions</li>
        </ol>
    </div>

    <h2 id="tier2">4. Tier 2: Incident Response & Investigation</h2>

    <h3>The Skill Jump</h3>
    <p>Tier 2 is where you transition from reactive monitoring to active investigation. You receive escalations from
        Tier 1, conduct deep-dive analysis, perform basic digital forensics, and coordinate incident response. This
        is the tier where most analysts either specialize or plateau.</p>

    <h4>Key Responsibilities</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Deep-dive investigation of confirmed incidents</li>
        <li>Endpoint forensics using EDR tools (CrowdStrike, Defender for Endpoint, SentinelOne)</li>
        <li>Network traffic analysis (Wireshark, Zeek, Suricata)</li>
        <li>Malware triage and basic reverse engineering</li>
        <li>Incident containment and eradication coordination</li>
        <li>Post-incident reporting and lessons learned</li>
        <li>Mentor Tier 1 analysts</li>
    </ul>

    <div class="technical-box">
        <h3><i class="fas fa-terminal"></i> Lab: Detecting Lateral Movement</h3>
        <p>Sigma rule for detecting pass-the-hash lateral movement via SMB:</p>
        <pre><code class="language-yaml">title: Potential Pass-the-Hash Lateral Movement

id: f9c2b8d7-3a1e-4b5c-9d6f-8e7c0a2b1d3e status: experimental description: Detects potential PtH via NTLM auth to remote SMB shares logsource: category: authentication product: windows detection: selection: EventID: 4624 LogonType: 3 AuthenticationPackageName: NTLM LogonProcessName: NtLmSsp filter: SourceNetworkAddress: - ‘127.0.0.1’ - ‘::1’ condition: selection and not filter level: medium tags: - attack.lateral_movement - attack.t1550.002 

    <h2 id="tier3">5. Tier 3: Threat Hunting & Architecture</h2>

    <p>Tier 3 analysts don't wait for alerts — they proactively search for threats that evaded automated detection.
        This tier requires deep adversary knowledge, custom detection engineering, and often overlaps with purple
        team operations.</p>

    <h4>Core Activities</h4>
    <ul>
        <li>Hypothesis-driven threat hunts based on threat intelligence</li>
        <li>Custom detection rule development (YARA, Sigma, Suricata)</li>
        <li>SOC process optimization and playbook development</li>
        <li>Threat intelligence analysis and adversary emulation</li>
        <li>Security architecture review and tool evaluation</li>
        <li>Purple team exercises with red team counterparts</li>
    </ul>

    <div class="exploit-box">
        <span class="exploit-label">HUNT EXERCISE: LIVING OFF THE LAND</span>
        <p>Hunt for LOLBin abuse — detecting attackers using legitimate Windows tools for malicious purposes:</p>
        <pre><code class="language-kql"># Hunt for suspicious certutil usage (T1105 - Ingress Tool Transfer)

DeviceProcessEvents | where TimeGenerated > ago(24h) | where FileName =~ “certutil.exe” | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ( “-urlcache”, “-split”, “-decode”, “-encode”, “http://”, “https://”, “-verifyctl” ) | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine, InitiatingProcessFileName | sort by TimeGenerated desc

Hunt for suspicious PowerShell downloads

DeviceProcessEvents | where FileName =~ “powershell.exe” | where ProcessCommandLine has_any ( “DownloadString”, “DownloadFile”, “WebClient”, “Invoke-WebRequest”, “IWR”, “wget”, “curl”, “Net.WebClient”, “Start-BitsTransfer” ) | where ProcessCommandLine !has “WindowsUpdate” | project TimeGenerated, DeviceName, AccountName, ProcessCommandLine

<h2 id="interview">11. Interview Preparation & Portfolio</h2>

<h3>Top 10 SOC Interview Questions (With Winning Answers)</h3>
<ol>
    <li><strong>"Walk me through how you'd investigate a phishing alert."</strong> — Start with email headers →
        check sender reputation → analyze URLs/attachments in sandbox → determine scope → contain → document
        IOCs</li>
    <li><strong>"What's the difference between IDS and IPS?"</strong> — IDS monitors and alerts (passive), IPS
        blocks threats (inline/active). Know where each sits in the network topology.</li>
    <li><strong>"How do you determine if an alert is a false positive?"</strong> — Correlate with multiple data
        sources, check baseline behavior, validate against threat intel, examine surrounding context events.
    </li>
    <li><strong>"Explain the MITRE ATT&CK framework."</strong> — Knowledge base of adversary TTPs organized by
        tactics (what attackers try to achieve) and techniques (how they do it). Used for detection mapping and
        gap analysis.</li>
    <li><strong>"What would you do if you found a C2 beacon on an endpoint?"</strong> — Isolate endpoint (EDR
        network containment) → preserve evidence → check for lateral movement → identify C2 infrastructure →
        scope the compromise → escalate for IR.</li>
</ol>

<h3>Portfolio That Gets You Hired</h3>
<ul>
    <li><strong>GitHub repo:</strong> Custom Sigma/YARA rules you've written with explanations</li>
    <li><strong>Blog posts:</strong> Document your home lab investigations (3-5 write-ups)</li>
    <li><strong>TryHackMe/LetsDefend profile:</strong> Show completion of SOC-focused paths</li>
    <li><strong>CTF write-ups:</strong> Document your problem-solving methodology</li>
    <li><strong>LinkedIn presence:</strong> Share threat intel analysis and industry commentary</li>
</ul>
